conclusion.justification: The report explicitly answers 'Yes' to the question and concludes that the body of evidence demonstrates widespread community mask wearing is an effective measure for reducing COVID-19 transmission.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
Yes, evidence indicates that masks can reduce COVID-19 infections when worn by a large proportion of the population. Multiple studies and systematic reviews support this conclusion:

- A systematic literature review published in MDPI found that masking policies and mask wearing are beneficial for preventing and reducing the risk of SARS-CoV-2 infections in various real-world settings (https://www.mdpi.com/1660-4601/22/10/1590).
- A large-scale study published in PNAS analyzed mask-wearing survey data from over 20 million people across six continents. It concluded that population mask wearing notably reduced SARS-CoV-2 transmission, with mean mask-wearing levels corresponding to a 19% decrease in the transmission rate (https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2119266119).
- A PNAS evidence review highlighted a World Health Organization-sponsored systematic review which found that "face mask use could result in a large reduction in risk of infection" (https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2014564118).
- A recent meta-analysis found that, after controlling for publication bias, wearing a face mask is associated with a reduced risk of COVID-19 infection by 11.8% to 28.5% (https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s41885-025-00185-5.pdf).

In conclusion, the body of evidence demonstrates that widespread community mask wearing is an effective measure for reducing the transmission of COVID-19.
